steps.label: 10M req/s hits the Global Load Balancer
CDN + edge cache absorb 94% of redirect reads
Write spikes safely buffered in Kafka
Sharded DB replicas stay within SLA

levels.title: Level 1: Client Ingress & Edge Layer
levels.description: Route global traffic safely and eliminate single points of failure at the entry point.

questions.text: Billions of users hit your shortener globally. What is the first infrastructure component that distributes traffic across healthy regions?
choices: A single Nginx server on one VM
A Global Load Balancer (DNS + anycast routing)
A monolithic application server
questions.correct_answer: A Global Load Balancer (DNS + anycast routing)
questions.explanation: A global load balancer removes the single point of failure at ingress and routes users to the nearest healthy region, improving both availability and latency.

questions.text: Most URL lookups are read-heavy and repeat the same popular links. Which edge component dramatically cuts redirect latency for hot URLs?
choices: CDN / Edge Cache
Write-ahead log on primary DB
Batch cron job every hour
questions.explanation: A CDN caches redirect responses at the edge, serving repeated lookups in single-digit milliseconds instead of round-tripping to origin.

questions.text: If one origin data-center fails, traffic must fail over automatically. What pattern prevents users from hitting a dead region?
choices: Health checks with automatic failover at the load balancer
Manual DNS edits during incidents
Retry loops in the mobile client only
questions.correct_answer: Health checks with automatic failover at the load balancer
questions.explanation: Active health checks let the load balancer drain unhealthy targets and route around failures without human intervention.
questions.uml_mutation:
cdn --> api[API Gateway]
    glb -.->|health check| api

levels.title: Level 2: Application & Caching Tier
levels.description: Decouple read/write paths and absorb traffic spikes before they hit persistent storage.

questions.text: Redirect lookups vastly outnumber URL creation. How should read traffic be served to protect the database?
choices: Route every read directly to the primary database
Front the service with a distributed cache (Redis/Memcached)
Store all mappings in local app memory on one server
questions.correct_answer: Front the service with a distributed cache (Redis/Memcached)
questions.explanation: A distributed cache absorbs the read-heavy workload, keeping hot keys in memory and shielding the database from flash crowds.
questions.uml_mutation:
api --> svc[Redirect Service]
    svc --> cache[(Redis Cache)]

questions.text: Creating a short URL triggers analytics, uniqueness checks, and counter updates. What decouples write spikes from synchronous API latency?
choices: A message queue (Kafka / SQS)
Synchronous two-phase commit across 5 DBs
Blocking the HTTP request until all analytics finish
questions.explanation: Queues decouple producers from consumers, letting the API respond quickly while background workers process durable side effects.
questions.uml_mutation:
svc --> queue[[Kafka Queue]]
    queue --> worker[Analytics Worker]

questions.text: Running one Redirect Service instance creates a bottleneck and SPOF. What is the standard fix?
choices: Horizontally scale stateless service instances behind the API gateway
Upgrade to a bigger single machine vertically
Move all logic into the database stored procedures
questions.correct_answer: Horizontally scale stateless service instances behind the API gateway
questions.explanation: Stateless horizontal scaling lets you add capacity elastically and survive individual instance failures without downtime.

levels.title: Level 3: Data Persistence & Consistency
levels.description: Design durable storage that scales past a single database node.

questions.text: A single relational database cannot store billions of mappings. What technique spreads rows across multiple nodes?
choices: Database sharding by hash of short code
One giant table with no indexes
Daily CSV exports to S3
questions.correct_answer: Database sharding by hash of short code
questions.explanation: Hash-based sharding distributes keys evenly across shards, letting write and read throughput scale linearly with cluster size.
questions.uml_mutation:
cache --> db[(Sharded DB Cluster)]
    worker --> db

questions.text: Cache misses still need fast reads without hammering shard primaries. What pattern offloads read traffic?
choices: Read replicas per shard
Disable cache and read primary only
Duplicate writes to every shard synchronously
questions.explanation: Read replicas serve cache-miss lookups from eventually consistent copies, preserving primary write headroom.

questions.text: Short codes must be unique at global scale without coordination hotspots. Which approach avoids a central counter bottleneck?
choices: Snowflake / base62 encoded distributed IDs
Auto-increment integer on one MySQL primary
Random 3-letter strings with no collision handling
questions.explanation: Distributed ID generation produces unique, dense keys without a single global sequence coordinator.

levels.title: Level 4: Observability & Resilience
levels.description: Close the loop with monitoring, rate limiting, and graceful degradation under chaos.

questions.text: A abusive client floods the create-URL endpoint. Where should rate limiting be enforced to protect the whole system?
choices: At the API Gateway before services
Only inside the database
Nowhere — rely on hope
questions.correct_answer: At the API Gateway before services
questions.explanation: Edge rate limiting stops bad traffic before it consumes downstream compute, cache, and database capacity.

questions.text: During an incident you must trace a redirect across CDN, service, cache, and DB. What infrastructure supports that?
choices: Centralized logging + distributed tracing (e.g. Prometheus + Jaeger)
SSH into each server and tail logs manually
Print statements in production only
questions.correct_answer: Centralized logging + distributed tracing (e.g. Prometheus + Jaeger)
questions.explanation: Unified observability correlates requests across tiers, shrinking mean time to recovery during outages.

questions.text: The analytics worker falls behind but redirects must keep working. What is the correct degradation strategy?
choices: Serve redirects from cache/DB; buffer analytics asynchronously with back-pressure
Return HTTP 503 for all redirects until analytics catches up
Drop redirect traffic entirely
questions.correct_answer: Serve redirects from cache/DB; buffer analytics asynchronously with back-pressure
questions.explanation: Critical user paths stay available while non-critical analytics lag safely in the queue with back-pressure controls.
questions.uml_mutation:
queue -.->|back-pressure| worker
    style cdn fill:#065f46,stroke:#34d399
    style db fill:#065f46,stroke:#34d399
